itens.titulo_original: Gaps in Current Chronic Spontaneous Urticaria (CSU) Management.
itens.resumo_original: Despite advances in therapy, chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU) remains a challenging disease with a significant impact. Although antihistamines, anti-IgE therapy and immunosuppressants form the basis of treatment, there are still substantial gaps in diagnosis, endotyping, prediction of therapeutic response and implementation of international guidelines. Newly licensed CSU therapeutic agents, such as Bruton tyrosine kinase (BTK) inhibitors and anti-interleukin-4 receptor alpha (anti-IL4Rα) agents, offer hope to patients who do not respond to treatment. However, we currently lack validated biomarkers of disease-specific features to determine which patient should receive which therapy, and the optimal positioning of these agents within the treatment sequence remains undefined. This narrative review examines the ongoing challenges in CSU management and proposes a more integrated, personalised and patient-centred approach.

ideia_conteudo.tema: Urticária crônica espontânea: por que cada caso é diferente?
ideia_conteudo.gancho: Você sabia que a urticária crônica nem sempre responde ao mesmo tratamento em todas as pessoas?
ideia_conteudo.mensagem_principal: A urticária crônica espontânea é uma condição de pele com causa não totalmente definida, que causa coceira e manchas (urticas) recorrentes por mais de 6 semanas. Embora existam tratamentos eficazes, a ciência ainda busca entender por que alguns pacientes respondem melhor a certas terapias do que outros.
ideia_conteudo.o_que_o_publico_precisa_entender: Nem toda urticária crônica é igual, e o tratamento deve ser individualizado por um dermatologista. Novos medicamentos têm surgido para casos mais difíceis, mas ainda não existem exames (biomarcadores) que digam com certeza qual remédio funcionará melhor para cada pessoa — por isso o acompanhamento médico contínuo é essencial.
ideia_conteudo.cta: Se você convive com urticária crônica, converse com seu dermatologista sobre as opções de tratamento disponíveis e tire suas dúvidas sobre o que esperar da evolução do quadro.
ideia_conteudo.fonte_medica: The British journal of dermatology (2026-10-03). DOI: 10.1093/bjd/ljag389 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42828452/
ideia_conteudo.origem: ia

itens.resumo: O artigo é uma revisão narrativa que discute os desafios persistentes no manejo da urticária crônica espontânea (UCE), apesar dos avanços terapêuticos com anti-histamínicos, terapia anti-IgE e imunossupressores. Os autores apontam lacunas no diagnóstico, na definição de endótipos da doença, na previsão de resposta terapêutica e na implementação das diretrizes internacionais. O texto menciona novos agentes terapêuticos aprovados para UCE, como inibidores da tirosina quinase de Bruton (BTK) e agentes anti-receptor alfa da interleucina-4 (anti-IL4Rα), como opções para pacientes refratários. Também é destacada a ausência de biomarcadores validados para guiar a escolha terapêutica individualizada e a falta de definição sobre o posicionamento ideal desses agentes na sequência de tratamento.
itens.titulo: Lacunas atuais no manejo da urticária crônica espontânea (UCE)
limitacoes: É uma revisão narrativa, não sistemática, portanto sujeita a seleção subjetiva da literatura pelos autores
Não há dados primários, estudos originais ou números apresentados no texto
Não foram informados detalhes sobre os estudos que embasam a aprovação dos agentes citados (BTK e anti-IL4Rα)
itens.por_que_importa: A urticária crônica espontânea é uma condição dermatológica comum e de impacto significativo na qualidade de vida. Compreender as lacunas atuais no manejo — incluindo a falta de biomarcadores e de critérios claros para escolha terapêutica — é relevante para a prática clínica em formação, pois orienta a reflexão sobre individualização do tratamento e expectativas realistas quanto a novas terapias.
itens.justificativa_ia: O artigo traz uma síntese atualizada sobre desafios no manejo de uma doença dermatológica prevalente e discute terapias já licenciadas, mas não apresenta dados novos de eficácia/segurança nem indica mudança imediata de conduta — é mais uma reflexão sobre lacunas e necessidade de personalização do tratamento, de valor para atualização profissional.

itens.titulo_original: Effect of Biologic Therapy on Depression and Anxiety Symptoms in Patients With Moderate-to-Severe Plaque Psoriasis: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
itens.resumo_original:
BACKGROUND: Various biologics are already widely used to treat patients with moderate-to-severe psoriasis, but there is currently a lack of comparative data on their effectiveness in improving symptoms of anxiety and depression.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate and compare the effects of biologic therapies on depression and anxiety symptoms in patients with psoriasis using a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
METHODS: We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials from inception to January 28, 2026. Randomized controlled trials and prospective comparative cohort studies in adults with moderate-to-severe psoriasis were included. Frequentist random-effects NMA was conducted at mechanism and drug levels, with network incoherence, sensitivity analyses, risk of bias, and certainty of evidence assessed. Skin-response associations and clinically interpretable psychological outcomes were additionally summarized.
RESULTS: Eight studies involving 4,319 patients were included. At the mechanism level, all biologic classes significantly improved depression and anxiety symptoms versus placebo. For depression, IL-12/23 inhibitors had the largest estimate [standardized mean difference (SMD) = 0.677, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.473, 0.881]; for anxiety, IL-23 (SMD=0.457, 95%CI: 0.304, 0.610) and IL-12/23 (SMD=0.457, 95%CI: 0.335, 0.579) inhibitors had similar estimates. At the drug level, several agents showed benefit, but rankings were uncertain because networks were sparse and certainty ranged from high to low. Within-study and exploratory comparison-level analyses indicated that psychological improvement generally accompanied skin improvement, yet the two were not strictly proportional.
CONCLUSION: Biologic therapy was associated with short-term improvement in depressive and anxiety symptoms in moderate-to-severe psoriasis, supporting mental health as a relevant component of overall treatment benefit. Psychological improvement generally accompanied skin response, while comparative differences across mechanisms and individual agents require confirmation in larger and longer randomized studies.

ideia_conteudo.tema: Psoríase e saúde mental: além da pele
ideia_conteudo.gancho: Psoríase não afeta só a pele — e o tratamento também pode ajudar na mente?
ideia_conteudo.mensagem_principal: Uma pesquisa recente reuniu estudos sobre pessoas com psoríase moderada a grave em tratamento com medicamentos biológicos (medicamentos que atuam no sistema imunológico) e observou que, além de melhorar a pele, esses tratamentos também estiveram associados a menos sintomas de ansiedade e depressão.
ideia_conteudo.o_que_o_publico_precisa_entender: É importante entender que essa associação não significa que o tratamento 'cura' a ansiedade ou a depressão, nem que toda melhora emocional depende apenas da pele. Os próprios pesquisadores destacam que a relação entre melhora da pele e melhora emocional existe, mas não é uma regra fixa — e que mais estudos, com acompanhamento mais longo, são necessários para confirmar essas descobertas.
ideia_conteudo.cta: Se a psoríase está afetando sua autoestima ou seu bem-estar emocional, vale conversar com seu dermatologista sobre isso — o cuidado com a pele e com a mente podem caminhar juntos.
ideia_conteudo.fonte_medica: The British journal of dermatology (2026-10-03). DOI: 10.1093/bjd/ljag435 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42828417/
ideia_conteudo.origem: ia

itens.resumo: Uma revisão sistemática com metanálise em rede avaliou 8 estudos (4.319 pacientes) comparando o efeito de diferentes classes de biológicos sobre sintomas de depressão e ansiedade em pacientes com psoríase moderada a grave. Todas as classes de biológicos melhoraram significativamente os sintomas de depressão e ansiedade em comparação com placebo. Inibidores de IL-12/23 apresentaram a maior estimativa de melhora na depressão, enquanto IL-23 e IL-12/23 tiveram estimativas semelhantes para ansiedade. A melhora psicológica geralmente acompanhou a melhora cutânea, mas não de forma estritamente proporcional, e as comparações entre fármacos específicos tiveram certeza de evidência variando de alta a baixa.
itens.titulo: Terapia biológica melhora sintomas de ansiedade e depressão em psoríase moderada a grave, aponta metanálise em rede
limitacoes: Número limitado de estudos (8) e amostra relativamente pequena para comparações em rede
Redes de comparação esparsas, levando a incerteza nas classificações por fármaco individual
Certeza da evidência variando de alta a baixa segundo o fármaco avaliado
Resultados de curto prazo; não há confirmação em estudos randomizados maiores e mais longos
Relação entre melhora cutânea e psicológica não é estritamente proporcional, sugerindo mecanismos não totalmente elucidados
itens.por_que_importa: O estudo reforça que o impacto psicológico da psoríase é um componente relevante do benefício terapêutico dos biológicos, ampliando a visão sobre o tratamento além do controle cutâneo. Isso é importante para a prática dermatológica, pois destaca a saúde mental como desfecho relevante a ser considerado na escolha terapêutica.
itens.justificativa_ia: O achado é importante para atualização profissional sobre o impacto dos biológicos na saúde mental de pacientes com psoríase, mas não constitui mudança imediata de conduta clínica, pois os próprios autores apontam incerteza nas comparações entre fármacos e necessidade de confirmação em estudos maiores e mais longos.

itens.resumo: A Anvisa proibiu a venda de determinados cosméticos e determinou o recolhimento de um gel falsificado. O texto disponível não traz detalhes sobre o nome do produto, fabricante, motivo específico da falsificação ou riscos associados.
itens.titulo: Anvisa proíbe venda de cosméticos e determina recolhimento de gel falsificado
limitacoes: O texto fornecido é apenas um título/manchete, sem detalhes sobre o produto específico, motivo da proibição, riscos à saúde ou abrangência da medida
Não foi informado o nome do produto, fabricante ou lote recolhido
Não há informações sobre os riscos concretos associados ao uso do produto falsificado
itens.fonte_primaria_titulo: Anvisa proíbe fabricação e venda de cosméticos irregulares
itens.divergencias: A nota oficial da Anvisa confirma a proibição da venda de vários cosméticos irregulares e a apreensão de um produto com rotulagem falsificada, mas esse produto é identificado como 'Profuse Nitrel Suavizante Balm' (um bálsamo), não como 'gel'. A manchete do Correio Sudoeste generaliza o item recolhido como 'gel falsificado', o que não corresponde exatamente ao nome/categoria do produto citado no comunicado oficial.
itens.por_que_importa: Medidas regulatórias da Anvisa sobre cosméticos e produtos falsificados têm relação direta com segurança do consumidor e podem impactar orientações dadas por dermatologistas sobre produtos de uso tópico.
itens.justificativa_ia: Trata-se de uma ação regulatória da Anvisa, que pode ser relevante para segurança do consumidor, mas o texto disponível é extremamente limitado (apenas o título), não permitindo avaliar o real impacto ou gravidade da medida para classificá-la como muito relevante ou relevante com segurança.

itens.titulo_original: Treatment of hypertrophic scars using fractional CO2 laser alone in comparison with adding botulinium toxin either intalesional injection or assisted drug delivery.
itens.resumo_original: Burns result in hypertrophic scarring, causing functional impairment, cosmetic and psychological concerns. Fractional CO₂ laser and botulinum, have shown promise in treatment. To evaluate the effectiveness of fractional laser treatment alone and combined with botulinum toxin A, delivered either through injections or topical application as fractional laser-assisted drug delivery in hypertrophic burn scar. A randomized comparative trial involving 16 patients with post-burn hypertrophic scars. The scar of each patient was divided into 3 sections: (1) fractional CO₂ laser combined with intralesional botulinum toxin type A, (2) fractional CO₂ laser monotherapy, and (3) fractional CO₂ laser with laser-assisted drug delivery of BTXA. Patients received three treatment sessions at monthly intervals, followed by a three-month follow up. Clinical outcomes were evaluated using the Vancouver Scar Scale. Intralesional BTXA demonstrated superior efficacy, achieving the greatest reductions in VSS (- 58.25%). Intralesional BTXA in combination with fractional CO₂ laser represents a highly effective treatment for post-burn hypertrophic scars, offering superior improvements in scar pliability, contour, and patient comfort compared with laser monotherapy or LADD. These findings support intralesional BTXA as the preferred therapeutic approach, while highlighting the potential of combination protocols for optimizing scar outcomes.

itens.titulo_original: Advances needed for improving leprosy diagnosis in Brazil.
itens.resumo_original:
INTRODUCTION: Leprosy remains a major public health challenge in Brazil, where delayed diagnosis sustains transmission and disability. Despite advances in diagnostic research, slit-skin smear microscopy remains the only laboratory diagnostic criterion recommended by WHO among the cardinal signs, despite its limited effectiveness. This diagnostic gap underscores the need to evaluate emerging and complementary approaches. Early and accurate case detection is central to the Global Leprosy Strategy and Sustainable Development Goals.
AREAS COVERED: This narrative review examines Brazil's leprosy diagnostic landscape, highlighting the strengths and limitations of the existing diagnostic pathway, including reliance on clinical expertise, limited access to complementary laboratory methods, and the impact of socioeconomic inequalities on timely case detection. It discusses emerging diagnostic technologies, including point-of-care tests, molecular assays, digital health, artificial intelligence, and precision public health, and their potential to improve early detection, particularly of paucibacillary disease and household contacts. It also emphasizes strengthening Primary Health Care, workforce training, contact surveillance, research, and stigma reduction to advance leprosy control.
EXPERT OPINION: Integrating innovative diagnostics with stronger Primary Health Care, workforce training, contact surveillance, research, and stigma reduction is essential. Equitable, evidence-based implementation can accelerate early diagnosis, reduce disability, and interrupt transmission in Brazil.

This diagnostic gap underscores the need to evaluate emerging and complementary approaches.

itens.titulo_original: The Formation and Reconfiguration of an Informal Medical Workforce: Hansen's Disease Patients Trained at the Sorokdo Medical Training School and Korea's Leprosy Healthcare System, 1950s-1980s.
itens.resumo_original: This article examines the Sorokdo Medical Training School (Noksan Medical Training School) and the lives of its graduates, focusing on their role in Korea's Hansen's disease healthcare system between the late 1940s and the 1980s. Existing studies have primarily portrayed Hansen's disease patients as objects of medical intervention, segregation, and state control. While such perspectives have illuminated the history of confinement, stigma, sterilization, and discrimination, they have paid relatively little attention to the active roles that patients themselves played within the healthcare system. By analyzing hospital records, government documents, overseas reports, and oral histories, this study reconstructs the experiences of Hansen's disease patients who were trained as medical personnel and explores their contributions to the operation of Korea's leprosy healthcare system. Established in 1949 at Sorokdo National Hospital, the Medical Training School was designed to address the severe shortage of medical personnel in Hansen's disease institutions and settlement villages. Graduates were deployed not only to Sorokdo but also to leprosy hospitals and settlement communities throughout the country, where they performed a wide range of medical tasks, including laboratory testing, drug dispensing, wound care, surgery assistance, rehabilitation, and outpatient treatment. In many settlements, where physicians were absent or visited only occasionally, they effectively functioned as the primary providers of everyday medical care. Their activities were therefore essential to both the treatment of Hansen's disease patients and the implementation of the state's leprosy control system. The article argues that these graduates constituted a form of "informal medical workforce" operating within, rather than outside, the state healthcare system. Although they acquired substantial clinical experience and were highly valued in practice, they were never fully recognized as professional medical practitioners. As Korea's healthcare system became increasingly professionalized from the 1960s onward, their broad medical responsibilities were gradually restricted. Yet their story was not simply one of exclusion. While some lost their positions within medical institutions, others adapted to the changing system by becoming leprosy control workers, laboratory technicians, radiological technicians, medical assistants, or operators of pharmaceutical sales outlets. Their experiences reveal how the professionalization of medicine simultaneously marginalized and incorporated non-professional healthcare workers. Methodologically, the study combines institutional records with oral histories in order to examine both the administrative position of these workers and their own understanding of medical expertise. The oral accounts show that graduates built practical competence through repeated clinical work, anatomical training, and the transmission of skills among senior and junior trainees, while official records and overseas reports reveal how heavily Hansen's disease institutions depended on their labor. The study also traces their divergent trajectories after the school was abolished in 1961. Some continued to work in Hansen's disease hospitals and settlement villages, whereas others moved into newly institutionalized occupations such as leprosy control work, clinical laboratory technology, and radiological technology. These trajectories demonstrate that professionalization did not simply eliminate informal practitioners; rather, it redistributed their skills across newly differentiated occupations and institutional boundaries. By recovering the largely overlooked contributions of these patient-medical workers, this study challenges physician-centered narratives of Korean medical history and reinterprets Hansen's disease patients not only as victims of modern medicine but also as active participants in the making of Korea's healthcare system. The history of the Sorokdo Medical Training School demonstrates that Korea's leprosy healthcare system was sustained not solely by licensed physicians and state institutions but also by the labor, expertise, and agency of Hansen's disease patients themselves.

itens.titulo_original: Off-Label Uses of Nemolizumab: A Narrative Review.
itens.fonte: Journal of drugs in dermatology : JDD
itens.resumo_original:
BACKGROUND: Nemolizumab, a humanized monoclonal antibody targeting interleukin-31 receptor α (IL-31Rα), is approved for atopic dermatitis (AD) and prurigo nodularis (PN) in adults and pediatric patients 12 years and older, following phase 3 trials demonstrating significant reductions in pruritus and disease severity in patients inadequately controlled with topical therapies. Emerging evidence has demonstrated rapid and sustained pruritus reduction in diverse pruritic conditions beyond its approved indications.
METHODS: We reviewed the literature from 2021 to 2025 examining off label nemolizumab use, analyzing case reports, case series, randomized controlled trials, and meta-analyses across dermatologic and systemic pruritic conditions.
RESULTS: Across 16 studies with diverse diagnoses, nemolizumab demonstrated consistent efficacy in multiple off-label conditions including cutaneous amyloidosis, lichen simplex chronicus, uremic and dialysis-associated pruritus, cholestatic pruritus, and refractory dermatologic conditions. Adverse events were consistent with those described in its package insert.
CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence supports nemolizumab as a promising therapeutic option for treatment-refractory pruritic conditions. The rapid onset, favorable tolerability, and broad efficacy across conditions with elevated IL-31 signaling suggest significant clinical utility, though larger randomized trials are needed for definitive recommendations. .

Foram analisados 16 estudos (relatos de caso, séries de casos, ensaios clínicos randomizados e metanálises) envolvendo condições como amiloidose cutânea, líquen simples crônico, prurido urêmico/associado à diálise, prurido colestático e outras dermatoses refratárias. Os autores relatam eficácia consistente nessas condições off-label, com perfil de eventos adversos semelhante ao já descrito em bula.

limitacoes: É uma revisão narrativa, não sistemática, o que pode introduzir viés de seleção dos estudos incluídos
Inclui relatos de caso e séries de casos, que têm baixo nível de evidência
Os próprios autores afirmam que são necessários ensaios randomizados maiores para recomendações definitivas
Uso off-label não possui respaldo regulatório para essas indicações
itens.por_que_importa: O nemolizumabe já é aprovado para dermatite atópica e prurigo nodular, mas o uso em outras condições pruriginosas ainda é off-label e carece de ensaios randomizados maiores e definitivos, conforme reconhecido pelos próprios autores.
itens.justificativa_ia: O tema é relevante para atualização profissional em dermatologia, pois sintetiza evidências emergentes sobre possíveis novas aplicações de um medicamento já aprovado para outras indicações, mas não representa mudança imediata de prática clínica nem aprovação regulatória, tratando-se de revisão de evidências preliminares e heterogêneas.

itens.titulo_original: Tralokinumab Versus Dupilumab for the Treatment of Atopic Dermatitis with Moderate-to-Severe Hand Involvement: A Matching-Adjusted Indirect Comparison.
itens.resumo_original:
INTRODUCTION: Both tralokinumab and dupilumab have shown efficacy in atopic dermatitis (AD) with moderate-to-severe hand involvement in double-blind phase 3 trials. As there are no head-to-head studies of tralokinumab and dupilumab, an anchored matching-adjusted indirect comparison (MAIC) was conducted.
METHODS: In the ADHAND trial, adults with AD with moderate-to-severe hand involvement were randomised to tralokinumab 300 mg or placebo every 2 weeks for 16 weeks. In the LIBERTY-AD-HAFT trial, adults and adolescents (≥ 12 years) with moderate-to-severe AD with hand and/or foot involvement were randomised to dupilumab 300 mg or placebo every 2 weeks for 16 weeks. An anchored MAIC was conducted using individual patient data from ADHAND weighted to match aggregate data for age, sex, race, and baseline Hand Eczema Severity Index (HECSI) score from LIBERTY-AD-HAFT, with placebo as the common anchor. Endpoints compared at week 16 were proportions of patients with Investigator's Global Assessment scores of 0/1, HECSI-75 and HECSI-90, and percent reductions in HECSI and the Routine Activity Impairment domain of the Work Productivity and Activity Index. Reductions in itch and pain and proportions of patients with ≥ 4-point itch improvement were also compared.
RESULTS: LIBERTY-AD-HAFT included 133 patients (dupilumab, n = 67, placebo, n = 66) while ADHAND included 235 patients (tralokinumab, n = 156; placebo, n = 79). The effective sample size after matching was 99 (tralokinumab, n = 76, placebo, n = 23). Anchor-adjusted relative treatment differences significantly favoured tralokinumab compared with dupilumab for the proportions of patients achieving HECSI-90 (17.5% [95% CI 0.8, 34.2]; p = 0.040) and decrease in percent routine activity impairment (16.0% [95% CI 4.8, 27.1]; p = 0.005). Relative differences for other endpoints favoured tralokinumab over dupilumab but were not significantly different between treatments.
CONCLUSION: In this anchored MAIC, tralokinumab was associated with a higher placebo-adjusted response than dupilumab, with a higher proportion achieving HECSI-90, and a significantly greater improvement in ability to perform regular daily activities versus dupilumab. Other endpoints were numerically in favour of tralokinumab. Graphical abstract and video abstract available for this article.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT05958407, NCT04417894. Video Abstract (MP4 112997 KB).

itens.resumo: Como não existem estudos head-to-head comparando tralocinumabe e dupilumabe, os autores realizaram uma comparação indireta ajustada por pareamento (MAIC) usando dados individuais do estudo ADHAND (tralocinumabe) e dados agregados do estudo LIBERTY-AD-HAFT (dupilumabe), ambos em pacientes com dermatite atópica moderada a grave com envolvimento de mãos, usando placebo como âncora comum. Após o ajuste, o tamanho amostral efetivo foi de 99 pacientes. Os resultados mostraram diferenças ajustadas por placebo favorecendo o tralocinumabe na proporção de pacientes atingindo HECSI-90 e na redução do comprometimento das atividades rotineiras, ambos estatisticamente significativos. Outros desfechos favoreceram numericamente o tralocinumabe, sem significância estatística.
itens.titulo: Comparação indireta ajustada por pareamento: tralocinumabe versus dupilumabe na dermatite atópica com acometimento de mãos moderado a grave
limitacoes: Trata-se de uma comparação indireta ajustada (MAIC), não de um ensaio clínico randomizado direto entre os dois fármacos
O tamanho amostral efetivo após o pareamento foi pequeno (99 pacientes)
Populações de origem diferentes (ADHAND avaliou apenas mãos; LIBERTY-AD-HAFT avaliou mãos e/ou pés)
Ajuste limitado a variáveis disponíveis (idade, sexo, raça, HECSI basal), podendo haver fatores de confusão não controlados
A maioria dos desfechos não apresentou diferença estatisticamente significativa entre os tratamentos
itens.por_que_importa: O acometimento de mãos na dermatite atópica tem impacto funcional relevante e opções terapêuticas comparativas entre biológicos ainda são escassas, já que não há estudos diretos comparando esses dois fármacos; esse tipo de análise indireta pode auxiliar na discussão sobre escolha terapêutica, mas não substitui ensaios clínicos comparativos diretos.
itens.justificativa_ia: Fornece dados comparativos indiretos entre dois biológicos já aprovados para dermatite atópica, com relevância para a prática clínica na escolha terapêutica em casos de acometimento de mãos, mas sem caráter de mudança imediata de conduta devido às limitações metodológicas da comparação indireta.

itens.titulo_original: INDIVIDUAL ARTICLE: Tildrakizumab for Real-World Psoriasis Care: Clinical Lessons From Medically Complex and Underserved Patient Populations.
itens.fonte: Journal of drugs in dermatology : JDD
itens.resumo_original: Tildrakizumab, a humanized monoclonal antibody targeting the p19 subunit of interleukin-23, has demonstrated durable efficacy and a favorable long-term safety profile in moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis. However, patients encountered in clinical practice frequently have comorbidities, treatment barriers, and social circumstances that are underrepresented in randomized clinical trials. This case review describes 16 patients treated with tildrakizumab across clinically relevant populations, including older adults, patients with cardiometabolic disease or complex medical comorbidities, and individuals with unique treatment considerations. Across these cases, tildrakizumab was associated with substantial improvement in psoriasis, including involvement of high-impact sites such as the scalp, nails and intertriginous regions. Durable disease control was observed in patients with prior malignancy, chronic infection, hepatic disease, cardiovascular comorbidities, polypharmacy, and prior biologic failure, without treatment-limiting adverse events attributed to tildrakizumab. In-office administration and every-12-week maintenance dosing also offered practical advantages for patients facing Medicare-related access considerations, self-injection aversion, inconsistent healthcare access, or adherence challenges. These cases demonstrate how tildrakizumab may be integrated into individualized psoriasis management and highlight its potential as a practical, effective, and well-tolerated treatment option across diverse real-world clinical settings.
itens.periodico: Journal of drugs in dermatology : JDD

ideia_conteudo.tema: Tratamento biológico para psoríase em pessoas com outras doenças de saúde
ideia_conteudo.gancho: Quem tem psoríase e outras condições de saúde também pode ter opções de tratamento?
ideia_conteudo.mensagem_principal: Pacientes com psoríase moderada a grave que também têm outras doenças, como problemas cardiovasculares ou hepáticos, muitas vezes ficam de fora dos estudos clínicos tradicionais. Relatos de uso na prática médica têm mostrado que certos tratamentos biológicos aprovados podem ser considerados nesses casos, sempre com acompanhamento individualizado.
ideia_conteudo.o_que_o_publico_precisa_entender: Biológicos são medicamentos que agem em partes específicas do sistema imunológico envolvidas na psoríase. Mesmo sendo aprovados, a escolha do tratamento ideal depende de uma avaliação individual feita pelo dermatologista, considerando outras doenças, medicamentos em uso e estilo de vida do paciente.
ideia_conteudo.cta: Converse com seu dermatologista sobre as opções de tratamento mais adequadas para o seu caso específico.

itens.resumo: O artigo descreve 16 casos clínicos de pacientes com psoríase moderada a grave tratados com tildrakizumabe, um anticorpo monoclonal que age na subunidade p19 da interleucina-23. Os pacientes incluíam idosos, pessoas com doenças cardiometabólicas, comorbidades complexas, histórico de câncer, infecção crônica, doença hepática, uso de múltiplos medicamentos e falha prévia a outros biológicos. Segundo os autores, houve melhora importante da psoríase, inclusive em áreas de difícil tratamento como couro cabeludo, unhas e dobras, sem eventos adversos atribuídos ao medicamento que tenham levado à suspensão do tratamento. A aplicação em consultório e a manutenção a cada 12 semanas também foram citadas como vantagens práticas para pacientes com dificuldades de acesso ou adesão.
itens.titulo: Tildrakizumabe no mundo real: série de casos em pacientes complexos com psoríase
limitacoes: Trata-se de uma série de apenas 16 casos, sem grupo controle
Não há dados quantitativos detalhados de eficácia ou segurança no resumo disponível
Resultados descritivos, sujeitos a viés de seleção e de relato
Não foi informado se há conflito de interesse ou financiamento da indústria
itens.por_que_importa: O texto traz dados de uso do medicamento em situações clínicas comuns na prática real, mas pouco representadas em ensaios clínicos controlados, como pacientes com múltiplas comorbidades e barreiras de acesso ao tratamento.
itens.justificativa_ia: Apesar de ser uma evidência de baixo nível metodológico (série de casos), o conteúdo é relevante para atualização profissional por ilustrar o uso prático de um biológico já aprovado em populações clinicamente complexas, frequentemente excluídas de ensaios clínicos randomizados, sem representar mudança imediata de conduta.

itens.titulo_original: Efficacy of Apremilast in Patients with Psoriasis with Limited Skin Involvement, Including High-Impact Site Involvement: A Pooled Analysis of Six Trials.
itens.resumo_original:
INTRODUCTION: Plaque psoriasis is associated with decreased quality of life (QOL) even in patients with limited skin involvement, particularly those with high-impact site (HIS) involvement. The efficacy of apremilast in patients with plaque psoriasis has been demonstrated in phase 3 and 4 clinical trials. Here, we evaluated the efficacy of apremilast across six clinical trials for patients with psoriasis with low affected body surface area (BSA), including patients with HIS involvement.
METHODS: Data were pooled across five randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials (patients were randomized to apremilast or placebo until week 16, followed by open-label apremilast) and one single-arm, open-label trial of apremilast for the treatment of plaque psoriasis. Patients in this post hoc pooled analysis had limited skin involvement (BSA, 3-10%), many with HIS involvement in the scalp, genital area, and/or nails. Week 16 and 32 assessments included BSA, Psoriasis Area and Severity Index (PASI), static Physician's Global Assessment, Dermatology Life Quality Index, and HIS-specific measurements. Nonresponder imputation was used for missing data for binary endpoints; a mixed-effects model for repeated measures was used to analyze continuous endpoints.
RESULTS: Of 1152 patients in this analysis (mean BSA, 6.3%; PASI, 6.8), those who received apremilast (n = 671) versus placebo (n = 481) had significantly greater improvements in skin clearance and QOL at week 16 (all endpoints assessed, p < 0.0001), with improvements generally maintained at week 32. Apremilast also yielded clinically greater improvements in patients with scalp, genital, and/or nail psoriasis at week 16 versus placebo (all endpoints assessed in affected patients, p < 0.01), with responses generally maintained at week 32.
CONCLUSION: Apremilast improved skin clearance and QOL at week 16, and responses were generally maintained at week 32, in a pooled population of patients with psoriasis with limited skin involvement, including HIS involvement. Graphical abstract available for this article. Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov identifiers-NCT03721172, NCT03777436, NCT03123471, NCT03774875, NCT02425826, and NCT03930186.

ideia_conteudo.tema: Psoríase não é só sobre 'quanto' da pele está afetada, mas 'onde'
ideia_conteudo.gancho: Você sabia que uma pequena área de psoríase pode impactar muito a qualidade de vida, dependendo de onde ela aparece?
ideia_conteudo.mensagem_principal: Áreas como couro cabeludo, região genital e unhas são consideradas de alto impacto na psoríase, porque mesmo com pouca extensão, podem causar grande desconforto físico e emocional. Estudos mostram que tratamentos já aprovados podem melhorar tanto a pele quanto a qualidade de vida nesses casos.
ideia_conteudo.o_que_o_publico_precisa_entender: A gravidade da psoríase não deve ser medida apenas pela porcentagem de pele afetada (BSA). Locais sensíveis, mesmo pequenos, merecem atenção médica especializada porque impactam significativamente o bem-estar emocional e social da pessoa.
ideia_conteudo.cta: Se você tem psoríase em áreas como couro cabeludo, unhas ou região genital e sente que isso afeta sua qualidade de vida, converse com seu dermatologista sobre as opções de tratamento disponíveis.

itens.resumo: Uma análise post hoc agrupou dados de seis ensaios clínicos (cinco randomizados, duplo-cego, controlados por placebo, e um de braço único aberto) com 1152 pacientes com psoríase em placas com área de superfície corporal limitada (3-10%), muitos com envolvimento em sítios de alto impacto como couro cabeludo, região genital e unhas. Pacientes tratados com apremilaste apresentaram melhora significativamente maior na clareza da pele e na qualidade de vida na semana 16 comparado ao placebo, com respostas geralmente mantidas até a semana 32. As melhoras também foram observadas especificamente nos pacientes com acometimento de couro cabeludo, genital e/ou ungueal.
itens.titulo: Análise agrupada de seis ensaios confirma eficácia do apremilaste em psoríase com área corporal limitada, incluindo sítios de alto impacto
limitacoes: Análise post hoc e agrupada (pooled), não um ensaio único desenhado para essa questão específica
Um dos seis estudos incluídos era de braço único, aberto, sem comparação com placebo
Texto não informa detalhes sobre características basais completas dos subgrupos de sítios de alto impacto
Texto não especifica eventos adversos ou perfil de segurança nesta análise
itens.por_que_importa: Reforça o uso do apremilaste como opção terapêutica para pacientes com psoríase de área corporal limitada, mas com impacto desproporcional na qualidade de vida devido ao acometimento de sítios sensíveis (couro cabeludo, genitais, unhas), população frequentemente subtratada por critérios de BSA isolados.
itens.justificativa_ia: Trata-se de dado de atualização profissional relevante sobre eficácia de medicamento já aprovado (apremilaste) em subgrupo clinicamente importante (BSA baixo, mas com sítios de alto impacto), contribuindo para refinar indicação terapêutica, mas sem configurar mudança disruptiva de prática clínica ou novo mecanismo/aprovação.

itens.titulo_original: Trial-derived body surface area rules may restrict access to topical precision therapies in vitiligo.
itens.resumo: Trata-se de um editorial publicado no JAAD International que discute como critérios de extensão de área corporal afetada, definidos originalmente em ensaios clínicos, podem estar limitando o acesso de pacientes a terapias tópicas de precisão para vitiligo. O texto disponível é apenas o título, sem resumo ou dados adicionais.
itens.titulo: Regras de área de superfície corporal derivadas de ensaios clínicos podem restringir o acesso a terapias tópicas de precisão no vitiligo
limitacoes: Apenas o título do editorial está disponível, sem acesso ao conteúdo completo ou aos argumentos detalhados
Por ser um editorial, representa opinião e análise crítica de quem escreve, não dados experimentais originais
Não há informações sobre quais terapias tópicas específicas são mencionadas nem sobre os critérios exatos de área corporal discutidos
itens.por_que_importa: A discussão levanta uma questão relevante sobre política de acesso a tratamentos dermatológicos, podendo influenciar como critérios de elegibilidade são aplicados na prática clínica e em decisões regulatórias ou de cobertura de terapias para vitiligo.
itens.justificativa_ia: O tema é importante para profissionais que acompanham o manejo do vitiligo, pois discute barreiras de acesso a tratamentos, mas por se tratar de um editorial de opinião sem dados novos, não configura mudança imediata de prática clínica.

itens.titulo_original: Baricitinib Efficacy Through 4 Years in Responders and Safety up to 5 Years in Adults with Severe Alopecia Areata: Final Results from BRAVE-AA1 and BRAVE-AA2.
itens.resumo_original:
INTRODUCTION: Long-term efficacy and safety data are imperative for therapies used to treat severe alopecia areata (AA) because the disease is chronic, loss of response can be devastating to patients, and the safety profile needs to support long-term therapy. Baricitinib, a selective JAK inhibitor, has been approved for severe AA in adults and is being studied in pediatric patients. This study evaluates the final long-term efficacy and safety of baricitinib in adults with severe AA.
METHODS: Efficacy was assessed for patients randomized to baricitinib 4 mg or 2 mg who achieved response (Severity of Alopecia Tool [SALT] score ≤ 20) at Week 52 (4 mg, N = 133; 2 mg, N = 72) and stayed on the same dose through Week 200. Proportions of patients maintaining a SALT score ≤ 20 and achieving a Clinician-Reported Outcome Measure for Eyebrow/Eyelash (EB/EL) Hair Loss™ score of 0 or 1 with ≥ 2-point improvement from baseline were reported using the modified last-observation-carried-forward method. Safety is reported as incidence rates (IR) per 100 patient-years at risk for the All BARI AA group (N = 1303) and Extended BARI AA group (N = 948) through 248 weeks of exposure RESULTS: For baricitinib 4 mg and 2 mg, respectively, among Week 52 responders, 115/133 (86.5%) and 61/72 (84.7%) maintained a SALT score ≤ 20 at Week 200. Regrowth of EB/EL hair continued beyond Week 52 and was maintained through Week 200. In up to 5 years of exposure with baricitinib, the IR for serious infections, nonmelanoma skin cancer malignancies, deep vein thrombosis/pulmonary embolism, and major adverse cardiovascular events remained low relative to background rates. No deaths occurred, and adverse event rates remained stable over time.
CONCLUSIONS: Within this population, ~ 85% of responders maintained SALT scores ≤ 20 through approximately 4 years with continued benefit for EB/EL. Baricitinib's safety profile remained consistent over 5 years of treatment, in line with prior BRAVE program findings.
TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: BRAVE-AA1, ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT03570749, start date, September 24, 2018; BRAVE-AA2, ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT03899259, start date, July 8, 2019.

itens.titulo: Baricitinib Efficacy Through 4 Years in Responders and Safety up to 5 Years in Adults with Severe Alopecia Areata: Final Results from BRAVE-AA1 and BRAVE-AA2.

itens.titulo_original: JAK Inhibitors for Alopecia Areata: Approved Therapies, Efficacy, and Unanswered Questions.
itens.resumo_original: Alopecia areata (AA) is a common autoimmune disorder characterized by non-scarring hair loss. While traditionally viewed as a T-cell-mediated disease, recent advances have elucidated the central role of the Janus kinase/signal transducer and activator of transcription (JAK/STAT) signaling pathway in its pathogenesis, establishing a self-sustaining inflammatory loop. The identification of this pathway has transformed AA from a condition with limited therapeutic options to one with targeted biological interventions. Over the past five years, multiple JAK inhibitors have received regulatory approval or shown promising results in clinical trials. Baricitinib, a selective JAK1/JAK2 inhibitor, became the first FDA-approved systemic treatment for severe AA, followed by ritlecitinib, which targets JAK3 and TEC family kinases and deuruxolitinib targeting the JAK1/2. Other agents, including ivarmacitinib, and the topical agent delgocitinib, are under active investigation, offering varying selectivity profiles and routes of administration. Compared with conventional therapies, JAK inhibitors such as baricitinib and ritlecitinib demonstrated therapeutic efficacy rates of 40-50% in Phase III clinical trials. Because head-to-head trials among JAK inhibitors in AA remain lacking, the comparative efficacy discussed in this review is derived primarily from indirect, cross-trial comparisons and network meta-analyses. Despite these remarkable advances, the field currently faces several significant challenges, including variable treatment responses, incomplete hair regrowth in patients with severe AA, potential long-term safety risks, and the absence of validated biomarkers to guide patient selection or predict therapeutic outcomes. Comparative efficacy, treatment challenges, and future directions including combination strategies and biomarker-guided therapy are also discussed to support informed clinical decision-making and highlight unmet needs in AA treatment.

itens.titulo_original: Relieving pain with OnabotulinumtoxinA in refractory burning mouth syndrome: protocol and outcomes of an exploratory case series.
itens.fonte: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
itens.resumo_original:
BACKGROUND: Burning mouth syndrome (BMS) is a chronic orofacial neuropathic pain disorder, occurring in the absence of clinically evident mucosal lesions or identifiable oral pathology that can explain the symptoms. A significant proportion of patients experience uncontrolled symptoms despite multiple therapies. OnabotulinumtoxinA (onaBoNT/A) is used in neuropathic pain, as clinical trials have shown benefits in peripheral and central neuropathic pain management with its application. We present an exploratory case series of four patients with refractory BMS treated with intradermal onaBoNT/A injections.
METHODS: Four patients with refractory BMS were included in this study. OnaBoNT/A intradermal injections were performed in the inner labial mucosae and tip of the tongue. We assessed pain intensity before the procedure and after 15 days, adverse effects, time to symptom recurrence, cumulative effects with multiple procedures, and patients' global impression of change.
RESULTS: All patients reported the procedure was quick and well tolerated. No immediate adverse effects were identified. All patients had significant pain reduction at 15-day follow-up assessment. Regarding adverse effects, one patient reported transient lower lip asymmetry in one procedure, and another reported transient mild mouth closure impairment. Symptoms recurred between 2.5 and 3.0 months after the first procedure. Three patients desired to continue the treatment. One patient reported no symptom recurrence after four procedures with three-month intervals; after four procedures, the treatments were suspended, and she remained asymptomatic until the end of follow-up. One patient reported incremental benefit from repeated procedures. All patients reported the treatment had a meaningful impact on their daily life.
CONCLUSIONS: Our results suggest that intradermal onaBoNT/A injections may constitute an effective and durable treatment option for patients with BMS refractory to conventional therapies. Despite these favourable outcomes, adverse events were noted in procedures targeting the labial mucosa. In future applications, we aim to examine technical variations between sessions associated with and without adverse effects, to optimise safety and refine the technique.

itens.resumo_original: Resultados postados. Fase: PHASE2. Status: COMPLETED. Patrocinador: Biosplice Therapeutics, Inc.. The purpose of this study is to characterize the safety, tolerability, and efficacy of topical SM04554 solution (0.15% and 0.25%) applied to the scalp of male subjects with Androgenetic Alopecia (AGA).

itens.titulo_original: A Study of SM04554 Applied Topically to the Scalp of Male Subjects With Androgenetic Alopecia Analyzed by Biopsy of the Scalp Prior To and Post Dosing
itens.resumo_original: Resultados postados. Fase: PHASE2. Status: COMPLETED. Patrocinador: Biosplice Therapeutics, Inc.. This study will assess the safety, tolerability, and efficacy of SM04554 at concentrations of 0.15% and 0.25%. itens.titulo_original: A Study Evaluating the Efficacy and Safety of SM04554 Topical Solution in Male Subjects With Androgenetic Alopecia
itens.resumo_original: Resultados postados. Fase: PHASE2, PHASE3. Status: COMPLETED. Patrocinador: Biosplice Therapeutics, Inc.. This multi-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study, conducted in Turkey, will assess the efficacy and safety of topical SM04554 solution (0.15% and 0.25%) applied daily to the scalp of male androgenetic alopecia (AGA) subjects.

ideia_conteudo.tema: Alopecia androgenética e novas pesquisas em tratamentos tópicos
ideia_conteudo.gancho: Você sabia que a ciência continua buscando novas soluções para a queda de cabelo?
ideia_conteudo.mensagem_principal: Pesquisas clínicas estão em andamento para testar novos tratamentos tópicos para alopecia androgenética, mas é importante entender as etapas desse processo antes de tirar conclusões.
ideia_conteudo.o_que_o_publico_precisa_entender: Um estudo clínico de fases 2 e 3 significa que um tratamento está sendo testado quanto à eficácia e segurança, mas ainda não é um tratamento aprovado para uso geral. É preciso cautela ao interpretar notícias sobre 'novos tratamentos' até que haja aprovação regulatória e publicação completa dos resultados.
ideia_conteudo.cta: Converse sempre com um dermatologista sobre as opções de tratamento disponíveis e aprovadas para alopecia androgenética.
ideia_conteudo.fonte_medica: ClinicalTrials.gov (2026-10-01). https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03742518
ideia_conteudo.origem: ia

itens.resumo: Trata-se de um estudo multicêntrico, randomizado, duplo-cego e controlado por placebo, conduzido na Turquia, que avaliou a solução tópica SM04554 (nas concentrações de 0,15% e 0,25%), aplicada diariamente no couro cabeludo de homens com alopecia androgenética. O status do estudo é 'concluído' e os resultados já foram postados no registro, mas o texto não detalha os desfechos de eficácia ou segurança encontrados.
itens.titulo: Estudo de fase 2/3 avalia eficácia e segurança da solução tópica SM04554 em homens com alopecia androgenética
limitacoes: O texto não apresenta os resultados numéricos ou conclusões do estudo, apenas informa que resultados foram postados
Não há detalhes sobre desfechos primários ou secundários, tamanho amostral ou significância estatística
Estudo conduzido em população específica (Turquia), o que pode limitar generalização
Não foi informado se há publicação revisada por pares associada ao registro
itens.por_que_importa: A alopecia androgenética é uma condição dermatológica comum, e o desenvolvimento de novas opções terapêuticas tópicas é de interesse para a prática clínica. No entanto, sem acesso aos resultados específicos (eficácia, segurança, comparação com placebo), não é possível afirmar se o produto representa avanço terapêutico.
itens.justificativa_ia: O estudo trata de um possível novo tratamento tópico para alopecia androgenética em fase avançada de pesquisa (fase 2/3), o que é relevante para atualização profissional em Dermatologia, mas não há dados suficientes no texto para indicar mudança imediata de prática clínica, já que os resultados detalhados não foram fornecidos.

itens.titulo_original: Pembrolizumab Combined With Cetuximab for Treatment of Recurrent/Metastatic Head & Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma
itens.resumo_original: Resultados postados. Fase: PHASE2. Status: COMPLETED. Patrocinador: University of California, San Diego. This is a prospective, multi-center, open-label, non-randomized, multi-arm phase II trial to evaluate the efficacy of combination therapy with pembrolizumab and cetuximab for patients with recurrent/metastatic HNSCC. There will be four patient cohorts, including a PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor-naïve, cetuximab-naïve arm (Cohort 1), a PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor-refractory, cetuximab-naïve arm (Cohort 2), a PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor-refractory, cetuximab-refractory arm (Cohort 3), and a cutaneous HNSCC arm (Cohort 4). A total of 83 patients (33 in Cohort 1, 25 in Cohort 2, 15 in Cohort 3, and 10 in Cohort 4) will be eligible to enroll. Patients will be enrolled at 4 sites: UC San Diego Moores Cancer Center, UC Los Angeles Jonsson Comprehensive Cancer Center, University of Michigan Comprehensive Cancer Center, and University of Washington Siteman Cancer Center.
itens.resumo: Resultados postados. Fase: PHASE2. Status: COMPLETED.
itens.titulo: Pembrolizumab Combined With Cetuximab for Treatment of Recurrent/Metastatic Head & Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma

itens.titulo_original: A two-hit mechanism triggers autoimmune hair loss.
itens.resumo_original: Autoimmune diseases arise from a breakdown of immune tolerance, yet the mechanisms that initiate tissue-specific autoimmunity remain poorly understood1-4. Here we identify a two-hit mechanism in which immune dysregulation and physiological neural activation converge to trigger autoimmune alopecia. We show that transient depletion of regulatory T (Treg) cells during the anagen phase of the hair cycle, but not during telogen, induces CD8+ T-cell-mediated destruction of immune-privileged hair follicle stem cells (HFSCs), resulting in hair loss. This anagen-restricted susceptibility depends on sympathetic nerve activity, which is physiologically elevated during anagen: sympathetic denervation prevents disease, whereas psychological stress or optogenetic activation of sympathetic nerves renders otherwise resistant telogen skin susceptible to autoimmune attack after Treg cell depletion. Mechanistically, sympathetic noradrenaline signalling through HFSC-intrinsic ADRB2 promotes physiological reactivation of endogenous retroviruses (ERVs) in anagen HFSCs. Under conditions of Treg cell depletion, this ERV-associated state drives autoimmune pathology by engaging AIM2-dependent innate immune activation and pathogenic CD8+ T cell responses. Accordingly, genetic ablation of Aim2 or pharmacological inhibition of ERV reverse transcription protects against disease development. Together, these findings show that physiological sympathetic activity establishes a transiently vulnerable epithelial state, whereas Treg cells prevent this state from progressing to tissue-specific autoimmunity. This neuro-epithelial-immune circuit links hair-cycle state to the breach of HFSC immune privilege and the initiation of autoimmune alopecia.

itens.titulo_original: Oral and Topical Spironolactone in Adult Female Acne: A Narrative Review Comparing Systemic and Local Approaches.
itens.resumo_original:
BACKGROUND: Adult female acne (AFA) affects 12-45% of women over 25 years of age and is frequently resistant to conventional therapies. The antiandrogenic properties of spironolactone have positioned it as a promising non-antibiotic alternative. While oral spironolactone has been increasingly studied, its topical formulation remains comparatively underexplored, and recent evidence syntheses have generally pooled both routes of administration rather than comparing them within a framework specific to AFA.
OBJECTIVE: This narrative review synthesizes and critically compares the available evidence on the efficacy, safety, and practical considerations of oral versus topical spironolactone in AFA.
METHODS: A literature search was conducted in PubMed and Google Scholar on 1 September 2025, using search terms combining adult female acne with spironolactone. Original clinical studies-randomized controlled trials, observational studies, and case series-were included. Preclinical studies, non-English-language articles, and non-original data were excluded.
RESULTS: Oral spironolactone (50-200 mg/day) consistently demonstrates significant reductions in inflammatory and non-inflammatory lesion counts and improves acne-specific quality of life. Head-to-head trials indicate comparable or superior efficacy relative to doxycycline, with longer treatment persistence than oral antibiotics. Topical spironolactone (2-5%) reduces comedones, papules, and pustules with minimal systemic absorption, suggesting a potential option for patients who are not candidates for systemic therapy. However, the evidence base for topical formulations remains limited by small sample sizes and heterogeneous study designs, and is derived largely from small mixed-sex or non-AFA cohorts and from pharmacokinetic studies in healthy volunteers; its applicability to AFA is therefore currently indirect and extrapolated.
CONCLUSION: Oral spironolactone is supported by robust evidence as an effective non-antibiotic option for AFA and is suitable for moderate-to-severe disease, whereas topical spironolactone appears promising but remains supported by limited and partly indirect evidence, derived largely from small and heterogeneous studies, and may be appropriate for mild-to-moderate acne or when systemic therapy is contraindicated. Because no head-to-head trial has compared the two routes, the comparison presented here is necessarily indirect. Future research should prioritize head-to-head comparisons of both routes and standardization of topical formulations.

itens.titulo_original: GLP-1 receptor agonists in psoriasis management.
itens.resumo_original: Psoriasis is a systemic chronic inflammatory skin disease associated with musculoskeletal, cardiovascular, metabolic, psychiatric, and gastrointestinal comorbidities. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) and dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP)/GLP-1 RAs have emerged as potential therapeutic adjuncts in psoriasis because, beyond their metabolic effects, these agents exhibit anti-inflammatory properties and may reduce expression of cytokines and inflammatory biomarkers. This review summarizes the current evidence from randomized trials and nonrandomized studies evaluating GLP-1 RAs and dual GIP/GLP-1 RAs in patients with psoriasis and discusses their potential role in disease management. Observational studies of liraglutide, semaglutide, exenatide, dulaglutide, and tirzepatide generally demonstrated improvements in psoriasis severity, body weight, metabolic parameters, inflammatory biomarkers, and quality of life, although most were limited by small sample sizes and uncontrolled designs. Randomized trials similarly suggest dermatologic benefit, particularly among patients with obesity and/or type 2 diabetes mellitus. Most notably, the phase 3b TOGETHER trial demonstrated greater skin clearance and weight reduction with ixekizumab plus tirzepatide compared with ixekizumab alone in patients with moderate-to-severe psoriasis and overweight or obesity. Complementary findings from the TOGETHER-PsA trial showed improvement in psoriatic arthritis disease activity as early as week 4, before clinically meaningful weight loss, supporting potential weight-independent anti-inflammatory effects of these agents. Future studies should include patients without obesity or diabetes to clarify the relative contributions of weight loss and direct anti-inflammatory effects to clinical response and determine whether the dermatologic benefits of GLP-1-based therapies extend to patients without underlying metabolic dysfunction.

itens.titulo_original: Staged Management of Vascular Occlusion With Ellansé (Polycaprolactone): A Modified Delphi Expert Consensus.
itens.resumo_original:
BACKGROUND: Vascular occlusion (VO) is a rare but serious complication of dermal filler injection. Current management protocols are derived primarily from hyaluronic acid fillers and rely on enzymatic degradation with hyaluronidase. Ellansé (PCL-CMC) is a poly-ε-caprolactone (PCL)-based filler composed of PCL microspheres suspended in a carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) gel carrier, neither of which is a substrate for hyaluronidase; a product-specific management approach is therefore required.
OBJECTIVES: To develop expert consensus recommendations for the recognition and management of VO associated with PCL-CMC.
METHODS: A targeted literature review (PubMed, January 2009-August 2025), in vitro rheometry and flow testing, and a three-round modified Delphi consensus process involving seven international experts were used to develop a staged management algorithm.
RESULTS: At 1:5 dilution, PCL-CMC viscosity decreased approximately 80-fold to near-aqueous levels; hyaluronidase solution conferred no additional benefit over saline alone. A full consensus or a consensus based on majority of the experts consensus (≥80%) was achieved on the majority of statements, including CMC-mediated obstruction as the primary mechanism, high-volume saline flushing with mechanical dispersion as first-line therapy, and retention of hyaluronidase in a supportive role.
CONCLUSIONS: This consensus-derived algorithm prioritizes reperfusion through dilution and mechanical dispersion rather than enzymatic degradation. Prospective clinical validation is required.

itens.resumo: Um grupo de sete especialistas internacionais conduziu um processo de consenso Delphi modificado, combinado com revisão de literatura e testes laboratoriais de reologia, para desenvolver um algoritmo de manejo da oclusão vascular (OV) causada pelo preenchedor PCL-CMC (Ellansé). Os testes mostraram que, na diluição de 1:5, a viscosidade do produto caiu cerca de 80 vezes, e a solução de hialuronidase não trouxe benefício adicional em relação à solução salina isolada. O consenso indicou a obstrução mediada pela CMC como mecanismo primário, recomendando lavagem salina em alto volume com dispersão mecânica como primeira linha de tratamento, mantendo a hialuronidase em papel apenas de suporte.
itens.titulo: Consenso Delphi propõe manejo escalonado da oclusão vascular causada pelo preenchedor Ellansé (policaprolactona)
limitacoes: Nível de evidência 5 (o mais baixo na hierarquia), baseado em opinião de especialistas
Os testes de viscosidade e fluxo foram realizados in vitro, não em contexto clínico real
Os próprios autores afirmam que é necessária validação clínica prospectiva
Consenso não foi unânime em todos os pontos, havendo apenas maioria (≥80%) em parte das afirmações
itens.por_que_importa: A oclusão vascular é uma complicação rara, mas grave, de preenchedores dérmicos, podendo levar a necrose tecidual ou outros danos sérios. Os protocolos atuais de manejo foram desenvolvidos principalmente para preenchedores de ácido hialurônico, que respondem à hialuronidase. Como o Ellansé é composto por microesferas de policaprolactona suspensas em gel de carboximetilcelulose — nenhum dos dois é substrato da hialuronidase —, esse consenso propõe uma abordagem específica para esse produto, o que pode orientar condutas de emergência em profissionais que utilizam esse tipo de preenchedor.
itens.justificativa_ia: Trata-se de uma recomendação de manejo para uma complicação grave e de risco à segurança do paciente (oclusão vascular), proveniente de consenso formal de especialistas, que pode orientar mudança de conduta clínica em situações de emergência relacionadas a um preenchedor amplamente utilizado, mesmo que o nível de evidência seja baixo e careça de validação clínica prospectiva.

itens.titulo_original: Regional photoprotection strategies in Indian Ocean phytoplankton: Arabian Sea vs South Tropical Indian Ocean responses to PAR/UVR stress.
itens.resumo_original: Phytoplankton photoprotection is a key yet understudied determinant of marine ecosystem resilience to climate-driven environmental stressors, particularly in the Indian Ocean (IO), where observational constraints limit projections of productivity under warming and stratification. While photophysiological adaptation has been extensively characterised in Atlantic and Pacific systems, IO phytoplankton communities remain poorly resolved. We assessed the photophysiological responses of natural phytoplankton assemblages from two contrasting IO bioregions-the productive, monsoon-influenced Arabian Sea (AS) and the oligotrophic South Tropical IO (STIO)-using onboard microcosm experiments that combined fast repetition rate fluorometry, HPLC pigment analysis, and microscopy. Surface and subsurface chlorophyll maximum waters were exposed to photosynthetically active radiation (PAR) alone or combined with ultraviolet-A/B radiation (PAR + UVR) for 72h under in situ temperature and natural light conditions. Dynamic photoinhibition, non-photochemical quenching (NPQ: xanthophyll cycle-mediated energy dissipation), and photoprotective pigment accumulation emerged as primary photoprotective mechanisms, but with distinct regional expression reflecting environmental stress gradients. In AS, rapid photoinhibition recovery (Fv/Fm returning to morning maxima by evening), antenna-associated NPQ, and inactive xanthophyll cycling characterised responses to high UVR stress. Conversely, STIO communities exhibited gradual recovery of photoinhibition, PSII reaction centre NPQ, and active xanthophyll cycle operation (diatoxanthin-diadinoxanthin) under sustained high-PAR conditions. These responses reflect the combined influence of physiological acclimation and community composition (AS: diatom-dominated; STIO: picophytoplankton-dominated), which indicates regional environmental gradients. Under projected surface-ocean stratification and mixed-layer shoaling, altered light climates and community restructuring will modify photoprotection mechanisms available to IO phytoplankton, with implications for primary productivity, carbon cycling, and ecosystem vulnerability to cumulative environmental change.

itens.titulo_original: Effectiveness of INTI educational program on photoprotection among adolescents in high-altitude rural Andean school: A quasi-experimental study.
itens.resumo_original:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effectiveness of an educational program (INTI) on knowledge, attitudes, and photoprotection habits among adolescents exposed to high levels of ultraviolet (UV) radiation in a high-altitude rural area of Peru.
STUDY DESIGN: Quasi-experimental. Pretest-posttest study with non-randomized control and experimental groups.
METHODS: The study included 37 third-year secondary school students from a public school in the Andean region of Peru, who were assigned to a control group (n = 18) or an experimental group (n = 19) that received the 12-session INTI educational program. Knowledge, habits, and attitudes toward photoprotection were assessed before and after the intervention using the CHACES questionnaire. Between-group differences in posttest scores were examined using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), adjusting for pretest score.
RESULTS: Pretest scores were similar between groups. At posttest, the experimental group showed higher mean scores than the control group in knowledge (M = 6.58; M = 5.89), habits (M = 12.7; M = 10.4), and attitudes (M = 33.2; M = 30.1). Analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) showed statistically significant between-group differences in knowledge (p = 0.033), habits (p < 0.001), and attitudes (p = 0.019) after adjusting for baseline scores.
CONCLUSIONS: The study demonstrated that the INTI program significantly improved posttest scores for knowledge, habits, and attitudes related to photoprotection in the experimental group compared with the control group.
itens.resumo: Um estudo quasi-experimental avaliou um programa educativo de 12 sessões (INTI) sobre fotoproteção em 37 estudantes de uma escola rural andina no Peru, expostos a altos níveis de radiação UV devido à altitude. Os alunos foram divididos em grupo controle (n=18) e grupo experimental (n=19), sendo este último submetido ao programa. Após a intervenção, o grupo experimental apresentou escores mais altos em conhecimento, hábitos e atitudes relacionados à fotoproteção, com diferenças estatisticamente significativas em relação ao grupo controle, mesmo após ajuste para os escores de linha de base.
itens.titulo: Programa educativo INTI melhora conhecimento e hábitos de fotoproteção em adolescentes andinos
limitacoes: Amostra muito pequena (37 participantes)
Estudo quasi-experimental, sem randomização verdadeira
Grupos não randomizados, o que pode gerar viés de seleção
Resultados baseados em autorrelato (questionário CHACES), sujeitos a viés de resposta
Ausência de seguimento de longo prazo para avaliar manutenção dos efeitos
População específica (adolescentes andinos), o que limita generalização
itens.por_que_importa: O estudo sugere que intervenções educativas estruturadas podem melhorar conhecimento e comportamentos de proteção solar em populações de alto risco por exposição UV elevada, como regiões de grande altitude. Isso é relevante para estratégias de educação em saúde e prevenção de danos actínicos e câncer de pele, embora não represente uma mudança de conduta clínica direta.
itens.justificativa_ia: O estudo é um quasi-experimento com amostra pequena e não randomizada, portanto não muda prática clínica nem representa evidência de alto nível. Ainda assim, é interessante do ponto de vista educacional, pois reforça a importância de programas de educação em fotoproteção em populações vulneráveis à radiação UV, podendo inspirar conteúdo educativo sobre proteção solar.

itens.titulo_original: Differential Expression and Correlation of High-mobility Group Box 1 and Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor Messenger Ribonucleic Acid across Leprosy Clinical Groups and Healthy Controls: A Cross-sectional Study.
itens.resumo_original:
BACKGROUND: Erythema nodosum leprosum (ENL) is an acute inflammatory complication of multibacillary leprosy. High-mobility group box 1 (HMGB1) mediates inflammatory signaling, whereas vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) regulates angiogenesis and vascular permeability. We compared whole-blood HMGB1 and VEGF messenger ribonucleic acid (mRNA) expression across leprosy groups and assessed their correlations.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 146 participants: 35 with ENL, 36 with multibacillary leprosy without ENL, 38 with paucibacillary leprosy, and 37 healthy controls. HMGB1 and VEGF mRNA expression was measured by one-step SYBR Green quantitative reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction. Group differences were analyzed by one-way analysis of variance with Tukey post hoc testing, correlations by Pearson's coefficient, and ENL versus multibacillary disease by multivariable linear regression adjusted for age, sex, bacterial index, and disease duration.
RESULTS: HMGB1 expression differed across groups (13.530, 12.478, 9.585, and 9.442; F[3,142] =1579.960; P < 0.001; η 2 = 0.971), as did VEGF (10.992, 9.885, 8.341, and 8.277; F[3,142] =656.570; P < 0.001; η 2 = 0.933). ENL showed the highest expression; multibacillary leprosy without ENL was intermediate, and paucibacillary leprosy did not differ from controls. After adjustment, ENL remained associated with higher HMGB1 (B = 1.223; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.907-1.539) and VEGF expression (B = 1.327; 95% CI: 0.991-1.662); both P < 0.001. HMGB1 and VEGF were strongly correlated within all groups ( r = 0.980-0.989; all P < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: ENL was associated with the highest HMGB1 and VEGF mRNA expression. Their strong co-variation does not establish a direct HMGB1-VEGF pathway or diagnostic validity.

itens.titulo: Differential Expression and Correlation of High-mobility Group Box 1 and Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor Messenger Ribonucleic Acid across Leprosy Clinical Groups and Healthy Controls: A Cross-sectional Study.
limitacoes: Estudo observacional: mostra associação, não prova causalidade.

itens.titulo_original: When "Leprosy" Is Not Leprosy by Polymerase Chain Reaction: Detection of Nontuberculous Mycobacterial Deoxyribonucleic Acid in Nasal Swabs from Patients with Chronic Skin Lesions in a Leprosy-endemic Area.
itens.resumo_original:
BACKGROUND: Leprosy remains a major cause of chronic dermatoneurological morbidity in endemic settings, and early etiologic confirmation is often challenging in primary care, where diagnosis may remain syndromic. Molecular testing can strengthen confirmation of Mycobacterium leprae , yet performance depends on specimen type and target selection, and leprosy-like phenotypes may overlap with cutaneous disease caused by nontuberculous mycobacteria (NTM). This study evaluated paired nasal versus buccal mucosal swabs from patients with chronic skin lesions and clinical suspicion of leprosy to characterize mycobacterial deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) signals using a stepwise molecular workflow.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study (September-November 2025) enrolled consecutive patients presenting to primary health centers (Puskesmas) in Palu City, Indonesia, with chronic cutaneous lesions (>2 weeks). Each participant contributed paired nasal and buccal swabs (140 specimens from 70 participants). DNA was extracted using a silica column method. Conventional polymerase chain reaction (PCR) targeting the M. leprae proline-rich antigen (PRA) gene was performed, followed - when indicated - by genus-level Mycobacterium 16S ribosomal ribonucleic acid (16S rRNA) PCR and additional species-associated targets; 16S rRNA-positive amplicons underwent Sanger sequencing with Basic Local Alignment Search Tool (BLAST)-based taxonomic assignment. Paired nasal-buccal positivity was compared using McNemar testing.
RESULTS: All mucosal specimens were negative for M. leprae by PRA PCR (0/140). Genus-level 16S rRNA PCR detected Mycobacterium spp. DNA in 20/140 specimens (14.3%; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 9.4-21.0) and in 20/70 participants (28.6%; 95% CI: 19.3-40.1). Positivity was substantially higher in nasal swabs (18/70; 25.7%) than buccal swabs (2/70; 2.9%), with discordant paired results and no participants positive at both sites (McNemar exact P = 0.0004). Sequencing produced valid BLAST similarity outputs in 19/20 positive specimens; closest matches were most frequently to Mycobacterium parmense (13/19; 68.4%) and Mycobacterium kyogaense (6/19; 31.6%).
CONCLUSIONS: In this endemic primary care cohort with chronic skin lesions, mucosal swab PCR targeting the single-gene PRA locus did not detect M. leprae , while a subset showed genus-level Mycobacterium DNA signals - predominantly from nasal swabs - with 16S rRNA sequences most closely aligned with uncommon NTM lineages. These findings support broadening diagnostic consideration beyond M. leprae when mucosal single-target PCR is uniformly negative. Because mucosal detection cannot establish lesion causality and partial 16S rRNA reads have limited species-level resolution, lesion-based sampling and higher-resolution confirmation (culture and/or multilocus sequencing) are warranted; escalation to more sensitive M. leprae targets (e.g., multicopy loci) may also be appropriate when clinical suspicion persists.

itens.titulo_original: [Reactional episodes in lepromatous leprosy: presentation of a clinical case].
itens.fonte: Revista de la Facultad de Ciencias Medicas (Cordoba, Argentina)
itens.resumo_original:
OBJECTIVE: to present a case of lepromatous leprosy with two reactional episodes during its course.
CLINICAL CASE: 32-year-old woman from Paraguay, who presented with retiform purpura followed by ulceration on the lower limbs, associated with altered thermal and pain sensitivity. She also had skin infiltration, malar region nodules, madarosis, and a saddle nose. The diagnosis of Lucio’s phenomenon in lepromatous leprosy was made through biopsy for histopathology and bacilloscopy. She began treatment with glucocorticoids and antimicrobials according to the WHO regimen, and subsequently developed an upgrading episode with worsening of previous lesions.
CONCLUSION: To highlight the importance of recognizing reactional episodes in order to initiate timely treatment and thus prevent severe disabling complications.

itens.titulo_original: Exacerbation of Bullous Pemphigoid following a Closed Bone Fracture in an Elderly Patient: A Case Report.
itens.resumo_original:
INTRODUCTION: Bullous pemphigoid (BP) is the most common autoimmune blistering disorder affecting the elderly population. While the etiology is predominantly idiopathic, physical trauma has been identified as a potential exacerbating factor. Most trauma-induced cases reported in the literature are associated with surgical incisions, burns, or open wounds. The development of generalized BP following a closed fracture, where the skin integrity remains initially intact, is an exceptionally rare phenomenon. The patient experienced a pre-bullous phase starting in June 2025, which significantly progressed to generalized BP following a closed radius fracture in October 2025.
CASE REPORT: We report the case of an 85-year-old woman who presented with a generalized blistering eruption 3 months after sustaining a closed fracture of the left radius. Physical examination revealed tense, fluid-filled bullae on an erythematous base involving the trunk and extremities. Histopathological analysis demonstrated a subepidermal blister with eosinophilic infiltration. The diagnosis was confirmed by direct immunofluorescence showing linear deposition of immunoglobulin G and C3 at the dermo-epidermal junction and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay detecting high titers of anti-BP180 autoantibodies. The patient was treated with a tapering course of systemic prednisone, initiated at 90 mg/day. This regimen led to the cessation of new blister formation within 2 weeks and complete clinical remission with normalization of inflammatory markers within 3 weeks.
CONCLUSION: This case highlights that closed skeletal trauma, even without surgical intervention, can serve as a precipitating factor for generalized BP. The mechanism likely involves the release of sequestered antigens and epitope spreading due to internal tissue damage. Clinicians should maintain a high index of suspicion for BP in elderly patients presenting with cutaneous eruptions following orthopedic injuries to ensure prompt diagnosis and effective management.

The mechanism likely involves the release of sequestered antigens and epitope spreading due to internal tissue damage. Clinicians should maintain a high index of suspicion for BP in elderly patients presenting with cutaneous eruptions following orthopedic injuries to ensure prompt diagnosis and effective management.

itens.titulo_original: Rapid Succession of Multidrug-Resistant Bacteremia and Candidemia in a Patient with Refractory Pemphigus Vulgaris: A Lethal Therapeutic Challenge.
itens.resumo_original:
BACKGROUND: Immunosuppressed patients with extensive skin barrier disruption face extraordinary risks for polymicrobial infections. The rapid, sequential emergence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteremia and candidemia in such hosts constitutes a particularly lethal complication with limited therapeutic options.
CASE PRESENTATION: We report a 74-year-old woman with refractory pemphigus vulgaris (PV), type 2 diabetes mellitus, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease who developed a cascade of MDR infections over a 14-day hospitalization. Following initial methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) skin colonization, she developed Serratia marcescens bacteremia, subsequently complicated by wound superinfection with carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB) and multiple Candida species, including the rare yeast Kodamaea ohmeri. Despite sequential antimicrobial escalation-from piperacillin-tazobactam/linezolid to meropenem/amikacin, and finally caspofungin-her condition deteriorated with diabetic ketoacidosis, culminating in the family's decision to pursue discharge with comfort care based on the patient's previously expressed wishes; she died three days later. K. ohmeri demonstrated reduced fluconazole susceptibility (MIC = 8 µg/mL), highlighting the diagnostic and therapeutic challenges posed by emerging fungal pathogens.
CONCLUSION: This case starkly illustrates the catastrophic potential of rapid, sequential MDR infections in profoundly immunocompromised hosts with skin barrier defects. It underscores the critical importance of early microbiological surveillance, the clinical urgency of dynamic antimicrobial stewardship, and the imperative for multidisciplinary management to navigate the irreconcilable conflict between necessary immunosuppression and life-threatening infection.

It underscores the critical importance of early microbiological surveillance, the clinical urgency of dynamic antimicrobial stewardship, and the imperative for multidisciplinary management to navigate the irreconcilable conflict between necessary immunosuppression and life-threatening infection.
